orientation.title: Passage orientation
orientation.meanSteepness: Mean steepness {{value}}° from level, ignoring whether a leg climbs or descends.
orientation.dipRefusedReason: This line work carries no altitudes, so nothing in it says whether a passage climbs or descends. Drawing it anyway would show the cave as level everywhere, which is a statement about the cave and not one this drawing can make.
orientation.noTrendTitle: No direction can be worked out
orientation.noTrendReason: Nothing in this line work runs anywhere on the map: every surveyed leg either drops straight down, climbs straight up, or is marked as passage already surveyed on another trip. A cave of pure pitches is the ordinary case for this. There is no trend to draw here, which is a statement about the line work and not about the cave — the lengths beside it were measured from the same survey and stand.

cave.title: Survey statistics
cave.nothingMeasured: This cave has no line work to measure. Nothing here is computed from a survey.
cave.notComputed: Not computed from this cave's line work.
cave.notDeclared: {{computed}} computed; nothing written in the record to compare it with.
cave.against: {{computed}} computed, {{declared}} in the record, a difference of {{difference}}.
cave.disagreementTitle: The survey and the record do not agree
cave.disagreementBody: A figure computed from this cave's line work differs from the one written in its record. Neither is automatically the wrong one: a typed-in morphometry is frequently older than the survey it is being compared against, and a survey can be incomplete. Check which is the more recent before changing either.
cave.basisSurveyFlags: Measured from the compiled survey, using the surveyor's own flags to decide which shots are passage. This is what these figures are defined as.
cave.hasAltitudes: This line work carries altitudes, so the vertical figures above are measured from it rather than assumed.
cave.noAltitudes: This line work carries no altitudes — a plan drawing of a cave is not a flat cave. Every vertical figure above is therefore left blank rather than shown as nought: nothing here says how far the cave descends, which is a statement about the drawing and not about the cave.
cave.measuredFromModel: Measured from the survey "{{name}}". A cave may hold several uploaded surveys, and figures taken from two different ones are not the same measurement.
cave.basisSkeletonHeuristic: Approximated from the stored centerline, because this cave has no compiled survey carrying per-shot flags. The shape of the line work stands in for the surveyor's flags: it keeps most of the surveyed length but drops loose shots at a station, and with them the last few metres of every dead end. These figures should not be set against a cave measured from its survey as though the two were the same measurement.

messaging.dailyPaidMessageCapHint: A carrier bills a text message by the segment, not by the message: 160 characters of the plain Latin alphabet travel in one segment, but a single accented letter re-encodes the whole message into segments of 70, so the same wording costs twice as much in Romanian as in English. An announcement that would take the day past this is refused outright rather than sent to half the roster. Segments already committed today count, including ones still waiting to go out.

hypsometry.nothingMeasured: There is no line work to measure.
hypsometry.noAltitudesReason: This survey carries no third coordinate, so there is nothing to distribute by height. A cave drawn in plan is not a cave lying on one level.

hypsometry.notConfirmed: No reading has been recorded yet

hypsometry.saveFailed: The reading could not be recorded. Reload and check what stands.
hypsometry.countedOverWhatYouMayPlace: Counted over the entrances you may place, which is deliberately not a count of the entrances in this area.
hypsometry.proposalIsNotAnAssertion: The levels drawn behind the bars are read off the histogram by arithmetic. They are a proposal about the measurements, not a statement about the cave.
hypsometry.springLinesExplained: The dashed lines are the altitudes of the springs in this area. A level cut at the height water leaves the massif at means something a level anywhere else does not.

structureComparison.noPassageTrend: This cave's line work has no measurable trend.
structureComparison.noStructureNearby: No fracture trace you may place was mapped within reach.
structureComparison.noStructureInArea: No fracture trace you may place was mapped in this area.
structureComparison.noDolines: No outline here has a usable alignment.
structureComparison.noDivergence: One side has nothing in it, so there is no disagreement to report. Nought here would claim agreement with a structure nobody has mapped.
structureComparison.divergenceScale: Nought means the two lie along each other; one means they lie across each other, a quarter turn apart.
structureComparison.linesOnly: Only mapped fracture and fault lines are compared. Bedding and joint readings taken at a station are a different kind of record and this installation stores none.
structureComparison.dolineModeElsewhere: The comparison of depression long axes against fault strikes is asked of an area, on that area's own page.

crossSection.title: Passage size
crossSection.noReadings: This cave's line work carries no wall distances. Nobody measured how wide or how tall the passage is, which is not the same as the passage having no size.
crossSection.volumeNotComputed: Not computed: no piece of passage has all four walls measured at both of its ends. Nought here would say this cave encloses no space.
crossSection.volumeScope: Computed over {{measuredLength}} of {{totalLength}} of passage — {{measured}} of {{total}} pieces. A station where a wall was never reached leaves the estimate rather than counting as zero, so this describes the part of the cave that was measured and no more.
crossSection.bandsNote: Each slice is {{height}} tall. A slice no station fell in is absent rather than drawn as passage of no size, and a station whose line work carried no altitude is in none of them.
crossSection.ratioNote: Above one is passage wider than it is tall; below one is a canyon.
crossSection.spreadNote: Each box is the middle half of the measurements, the line across it the median, and the whiskers the smallest and largest. A slice of the cave nobody measured leaves a gap rather than a box on the floor of the axis.
crossSection.scalingValue: height rises as width to the power {{exponent}}
crossSection.scalingFit: over {{count}} stations, accounting for {{r2}} of the spread
crossSection.scalingNote: A power near one is a cave whose large passages are scaled-up copies of its small ones; below one it widens faster than it heightens, above one it heightens faster. It describes the measured dimensions and estimates no discharge.

passagePattern.title: What the shape suggests
passagePattern.notAnAssertion: The pattern below is read off the measurements by rules whose thresholds are chosen conventions, not measurements. It is a proposal about this survey, not a statement about the cave — which is why every rule is shown, including the ones that looked and stayed silent.
passagePattern.rulesTitle: Every rule, and what it did
passagePattern.assessed: {{fired}} of {{assessable}} rules that could be assessed fired. {{assessable}} of {{total}} rules had figures to read.
passagePattern.networkFigures: {{nodes}} places passages meet or end, {{loops}} independent loops, {{ends}} dead ends.

rule.networkIsLooped: The network closes on itself often
rule.networkIsTreeLike: The network barely closes on itself
rule.networkEndsOften: Much of the network is where the survey stopped
rule.networkRings: Passages leaving a junction are themselves joined
rule.bearingsAreConcentrated: The passage runs on a small number of trends
rule.passageIsSteep: The passage is steep on average
rule.passageIsLevel: The passage is level and the cave gains little height
rule.profileOscillates: The passage climbs and descends while the cave stays near one level
rule.sectionIsWide: The cross-section is wider than it is tall
rule.sectionIsTall: The cross-section is taller than it is wide

figure.verticality: Height gained per metre of passage

caveat.figuresAreApproximated: The figures were approximated from the stored centerline rather than taken from the surveyor's own per-shot flags, so this suggestion rests on a guess for a measurement.
caveat.networkIsIncomplete: Reading the survey file lost legs or merged stations, so the network described here is smaller than the one that was surveyed.
caveat.networkCompletenessIsUnknown: Nothing records whether reading the survey file lost anything, which is not the same as nothing having been lost.
caveat.noAltitudes: The line work carries no altitudes, so every rule about the profile had nothing to read.
caveat.noCrossSections: No station measured a complete cross-section, so the rules about passage shape had nothing to read.
caveat.noNetworkFigures: The passage network was never measured, so the rules about its shape had nothing to read.
